summary: Riverview Health and Redwood reviewed security posture, data handling and privacy controls focused on prompt/content retention, PII/PHI handling, encryption/KMS, RBAC/SSO, audit logs, and 'no training on customer data' assurances. Next steps: send SOC2/ISO docs, schedule technical deep dive for KMS and private deployment, and agree pilot retention settings.
topics: PII/PHI handling and HIPAA / BAA implications
Encryption at rest/in transit, KMS/HSM options
RBAC, SSO/SAML integration and audit logs
transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. We're on for 50 minutes, agenda is SOC2/ISO, data handling, encryption/KMS, and the retention questions you sent.
[00:09] Karen (Riverview): Great thanks. We have Dr. Patel, Lena from compliance, and Marco, our ML engineer. Trying to move to a pilot but compliance needs clarity on PHI/PII handling and whether Redwood ever uses customer prompts to train models.
[00:20] Maya: Totally understandable. I'll hand to Elliot to run the technical side then we can cover contract questions.
[00:25] Elliot (Redwood SE): Hi all, quick note up front: Redwood's standard position is that hosted API customers' content may be processed for service improvement unless contractually exempted; for enterprise pilots we can disable retention and we have private deployments where customer data never leaves their VPC. Important to distinguish hosted vs dedicated vs private.
[00:42] Lena (Compliance): Can you clarify "processed for service improvement"? We need a clear yes/no on training.
[00:47] Elliot: Right. To be precise: by default, some metadata may be used to improve systems, but we have clear offerings for Dedicated and Private deployments we provide contractual commitments that customer prompt/content is not used to train models. For hosted, we can provide opt-outs and a retention window.
[01:05] Karen: What's the default retention window on hosted?
[01:08] Maya: Default is 30 days for prompt/content in logs, primarily for debugging and fraud detection, but it can be reduced or disabled for enterprise customers under contract.
[01:17] Marco: If we start a pilot on hosted API, how do we guarantee PHI isn't retained? We can't risk exposure.
[01:23] Elliot: For PHI heavy workloads we typically recommend either Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity with data isolation) or Private (VPC/on-prem). Both support disabling retention and we can route logs to your logging account or S3 with customer-side KMS.
[01:36] Dr. Patel: We also need to confirm BAA support and whether Redwood signs a BAA for HIPAA workloads.
[01:40] Jordan (Redwood CSM): We do engage on BAAs with enterprise customers; it's supported and we can bring legal to the table. We'll share the standard BAA template as part of next steps.
[01:49] Lena: Audit logs what level do you capture? We need per-request tracing, user identity, and model versioning for auditability.
[01:56] Elliot: We capture request-level logs including timestamp, route, model version, token counts, and request IDs. For hosted we store them centrally; for Dedicated/Private we can push logs into your cloud account or provide log streaming. RBAC ties into this our Console exposes role-based access controls and SSO via SAML/OAuth.
[02:16] Karen: Do you retain full prompt text in those logs or a hash?
[02:20] Elliot: By default, logs include full prompt text (to aid debugging) but for enterprise we can configure redaction or tokenization, or route raw logs to your environment only. We can also keep only hashes in Redwood's system.
[02:31] Marco: KMS question can we bring our own key? We require customer-managed keys for encryption at rest.
[02:36] Elliot: Yes, BYOK is supported for Dedicated and Private. For hosted we offer envelope encryption where you manage the master key in KMS and we use a data key. HSM integration is available on the private stack.
[02:48] Lena: And for in-transit encryption? TLS is fine but do you support mutual TLS?
[02:52] Maya: We support TLS1.2/1.3 for all traffic and can enable mTLS for private endpoints in Dedicated/Private setups.
[02:59] Karen: About SSO we use Okta. Can you integrate with SAML SSO and SCIM for provisioning?
[03:05] Jordan: Yes, SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning are supported, and we have RBAC roles (admin, dev, viewer) that map to SAML groups. We'll share the integration guide.
[03:15] Dr. Patel: We need a contractual assurance that data won't be used to train models. How is that stated?
[03:20] Maya: For Dedicated/Private it's standard to include a clause: "Customer data will not be used to train or improve models". For hosted we can negotiate an addendum or opt-out that disables retention and training use. We'll attach example language.
[03:33] Lena: Are there any residual learnings or aggregated telemetry retained by Redwood that could imply customer-specific behavior?
[03:40] Elliot: We collect aggregate usage metrics for capacity planning these are coarse (token volumes, latency distributions) and stripped of identifiers. We can exclude particular clients on request.
[03:50] Karen: Encryption key rotation policy? If we manage keys, how often do you rotate or allow rotation?
[03:56] Elliot: Customers control rotation cadence in their KMS. For Redwood-managed keys we rotate on a quarterly schedule and track key versions; rotation is compatible with our envelope encryption scheme.
[04:07] Marco: About audit logs retention  compliance wants 7 years for certain items; can you export logs to our archival?
[04:12] Maya: Yes, logs can be streamed to your archive (S3/Blob) and you control retention there. Redwood's default retention is configurable independently.
[04:20] Lena: What about redaction of PII in transcripts returned to our front end? Can Redwood provide automated PII scrubbers?
[04:27] Elliot: We have built-in PII detection and can auto-mask or redact tokens server-side. For highest assurance you can do client-side scrub before sending. We'll demonstrate masking in the demo.
[04:38] Karen: Ok can you confirm SOC 2 and ISO posture?
[04:41] Maya: We're SOC 2 Type II compliant and have an ISO27001 summary. We'll share the certs and the SOC 2 report under NDA.
[04:49] Lena: Any penetration test results?
[04:51] Jordan: We perform regular pentests and can share executive summaries; full reports require an NDA.
[04:57] Marco: Latency vs dedicated isolation tradeoff  if we go private, what's the performance hit?
[05:02] Elliot: For Private deployments within your region, performance is comparable; the main tradeoffs are operational overhead and initial setup time. Dedicated reserved capacity gives the same runtime but with Redwood-managed infra and SLA.
[05:14] Dr. Patel: One more on model training: even if you say you don't train, do you collect embeddings or feature hashes that could be examined to reconstruct examples?
[05:22] Elliot: We do not store embeddings for hosted enterprise customers by default; for hosted they may be stored for indexing features unless disabled. For Dedicated/Private we can disable embeddings persistence entirely or route them to your storage.
[05:36] Maya: Quick recap we'll send SOC2/ISO docs, example BAA, KMS notes, and propose pilot SoW with retention disabled. We'll also schedule a deep technical session to walk through private/Dedicated architecture.
[05:47] Karen: Sounds good. Lena will collate a short list of acceptance criteria for the pilot and share back.
[05:53] Lena: Yes, I'll send over compliance checklist items.
[05:56] Maya: Great thanks everyone. We'll follow up by email with the artifacts and proposed meeting times.
[05:59] Dr. Patel: Thanks all.
[06:02] [call ends]

Notes on transcript: transcription contains occasional mis-hearings and shorthand; speaker labels are best effort.
